drafts.angle: Primitive thesis (rides @rauchg's 'Traces are the essential new primitive', 119K and 869 bookmarks)
drafts.draft_en:
Traces are the new primitive for code.

They'll be the new primitive for ads too.

Every AI creative should ship with its trace:
→ the prompt
→ the model
→ every claim it makes
→ every brand, legal and platform rule it was checked against
→ who approved it

If you can't trace an ad, you can't defend it.
drafts.video_tip: 20s vertical: a finished ad on screen, then 'peel back' layers one by one (prompt → model → claims → rule checks → approver) as arrow-list text. End on the last line. Use only your own ads and real Aubric product footage.

drafts.angle: Numbered playbook (rides @gregisenberg's 'open sourcing your saas is the new saas playbook', 2.3K bookmarks, ~2x likes)
drafts.draft_en:
The new ad-ops playbook:

1. Write your brand rules down like code, not a PDF
2. Add the legal claims you can and can't make
3. Add each ad platform's policy
4. Run every AI creative against all three before it ships
5. Approve, fix, or block. In minutes, not review rounds

The teams that do this will ship 10x more ads without 10x more risk.
drafts.video_tip: 25s screen-recording style: numbers 1-5 stack on screen as you talk; on step 4 cut to a real Aubric run returning APPROVE / FIX / BLOCK. Keep captions burned in for silent autoplay.

drafts.angle: Old way / new way (rides @rauchg's 'users are agents, you run evals', 453 bookmarks on 43K)
drafts.draft_en:
The old way: make the ad, send it to legal, wait 3 rounds of email, launch, get flagged anyway.

The new way: brand, claims and platform rules run as evals on every creative before it ships.

Review is becoming an eval loop.
drafts.video_tip: 12s split screen: left 'old way' (email thread piling up, a 'rejected' notice), right 'new way' (a creative scored and approved before publish). Hold the last line as text for 3s.
